--- title: "September 23, 2026" date: 2026-09-23 description: "Network median 0.08 in (range 0.00–2.36 in); peak IVT 68 kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹ from the SW" categories: [IVT < 250, Final] execute: freeze: auto --- ## Summary Across 39 gauges the event total ranged from 0.00 to 2.36 in (median 0.08 in). The central 80% of the network-mean rain fell between Sep 23 11:00 MST and Sep 23 15:00 MST (4 h). Moisture transport over Flagstaff stayed below atmospheric-river strength: ERA5 IVT peaked at 68 kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹ from the SW at Sep 23 05:00 MST, and total column water vapour reached 18 mm. At the IVT peak, 500-hPa flow over Flagstaff was from the SW at 9 m s⁻¹, and the 500-hPa trough axis along 35.25°N was at 115.2°W, 327 km west of Flagstaff (5,824 m, against 5,834 m over Flagstaff). A closed 500-hPa low (5,815 m) was centred 1,060 km to the SW, at 28.0°N 119.0°W. The strongest 250-hPa wind within 1,000 km was 49 m s⁻¹, 887 km to the NNE. The 250-hPa wind over Flagstaff peaked at 31 m s⁻¹ (Sep 23 05:00 MST), at the same time as the IVT peak. ## Rain across the network ::: {#cbcdd7ea .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Event rain total at each city and county gauge (circle area proportional to total, labels in inches) over shaded relief (USGS 3DEP), 200-m elevation contours, streams (USGS NHD) and highways (Census TIGER). Excerpts, quoted verbatim (links to the Iowa Environmental Mesonet archive): - **Sep 23, 2:56 AM MST** ([AFD](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=AFDFGZ&e=202609230956)): "A significant plume of deep monsoon moisture continues to flow northward into New Mexico, with widespread rain and thunderstorms. Over northern Arizona, drier air remains for much of Coconino/Yavapai counties early this morning, with dewpoints in the 30s/40s." - **Sep 23, 12:14 PM MST** ([AFD](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=AFDFGZ&e=202609231914)): "Moisture continues to stream into Arizona, as deep and layered southwest flow persists over the southwest United States.
